answer.answer: No. kg never calls an LLM nor needs API keys (decision:no-embedded-llm, RF-24, which justifies package:kg). Documents, decisions and concepts are read by an external AI agent (e.g. Claude Code) that uses kg as a tool: following the agent guide shipped in package:kg.agents (RF-20, read with `kg guide`, exported as the kg-graph skill via `kg guide --skill`), the agent reads the repo's docs and writes JSON that conforms to the schema, with provenance method `llm` and a confidence, validates it with `kg validate`, and loads it with `kg add`, which merges it into the .kg store by ID (kg.merge.add_to_store, RF-21/RF-30). On merge, parser provenance wins over llm provenance (decision:parser-wins-over-llm). The parser (`kg extract`) only produces the code-derived layer.
